title: Add pcb_bend and pcb_stiffener elements for flex PCBs
description: Add pcb_bend and pcb_stiffener schemas and types to describe bends and bonded reinforcement in flex PCB designs, ensuring flat layout preservation and unit-aware validation.
body:
Flex PCB designs need to describe bends and bonded reinforcement while preserving their flat layout. Add `pcb_bend` and `pcb_stiffener` schemas and types, export them publicly, and register them in `any_circuit_element` and `PcbCircuitElement`.

- Bends carry a board reference, directed `start`/`end` centerline, signed target angle, neutral-surface radius, and moving side.
- Stiffeners carry a board reference, rectangle or resolved polygon geometry, attachment face, material, and separate material/adhesive thicknesses. They do not add copper layers.
- Unit-aware validation rejects degenerate bends, nonfinite/nonpositive dimensions, zero-area polygons, and conflicting shape geometry. Standard generated IDs and optional ownership/name metadata are supported.

Coordinates on these new records are relative to the flat board center. The documentation defines the runtime contract: flat/folded rendering derives CAD positions and orientations without overwriting stored PCB geometry or flat CAD poses. This PR does not implement folding, rendering settings, board material changes, or regional rigid-flex stackups.

Includes examples, coordinate/normalization documentation, and 10 tests covering parsing, validation, public exports, union membership, and JSON round trips. Corresponding TSX props: https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/864.

Validation: all 381 tests pass; TypeScript check, ESM/declaration build, Zod lint, snake-case check, changed-file formatting, and diff whitespace checks pass. Generated README output was reviewed; unrelated regeneration changes were excluded and the stiffener variants are documented explicitly.

body:
Flex boards currently have no props contract for intended bends or bonded reinforcement. Add exported `PcbBendProps` / `pcbBendProps` and `PcbStiffenerProps` / `pcbStiffenerProps` for `<pcbbend />` and `<pcbstiffener />`.

Bends specify a directed centerline, signed angle, neutral-surface radius, and moving side. Stiffeners support rectangular or polygon geometry, existing PCB placement props, an explicit attachment face/material, and separate material/adhesive thicknesses. Unit-aware parsers reject degenerate centerlines, nonfinite/nonpositive dimensions, degenerate polygon area, and conflicting shape geometry. No important design values are defaulted.

`docs/flex-pcb.md` defines coordinate and normalization semantics and shows two reinforced component sections joined by a flex bridge. It distinguishes bonded stiffeners from integrated rigid-flex stackups and includes a clearly marked future regional-stackup sketch. This PR supplies props only; core JSX registration, Circuit JSON, folding/rendering, board-level DRC, and fabrication exports remain downstream work.

Large imported boards eagerly build a named phase-state map for every renderable. AM62A has 39,779 renderables, and none of those maps are inspected during its normal unobserved render.

Keep ordinary `{ initialized, dirty }` objects in an indexed array. Build the public named map only on first access, using references to those same objects. Render methods directly assign `phaseState.initialized` and `phaseState.dirty`: no packed flags, boolean-array synchronization, state reconstruction, or setter helpers. Once the map is exposed, read it to preserve callers replacing individual entries or the entire map.

Also avoid temporary arrays when checking previous async effects, check the isolated phase before component fields, and skip lifecycle event preparation when no listeners exist. Phase ordering, async barriers, live subscriptions and custom-root/debug behavior are preserved.

Three fresh processes per variant on the frozen AM62A input, in rotating order, with pours disabled:

| Variant | Eval + core render median | Peak RSS median |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Merged #4093 baseline | 5.896 s | 1,032 MiB |
| Previous boolean arrays | 4.898 s | 801 MiB |
| Shared state objects | 4.970 s | 884 MiB |

The simpler code retains a **15.7% improvement over baseline** in this batch. It takes **0.072 s (1.5%) longer** and about **83 MiB more peak process memory** than boolean arrays. All nine outputs match: 66,219 records, normalizing only software-version metadata. Timings exclude module startup, serialization, transfer and viewer rendering. The 2-second target remains unmet.

title: Fix net lookup costs across the full render lifecycle
description: Fixes net lookup costs across the full render lifecycle by optimizing the net resolution process, resulting in significant performance improvements during rendering.
body:
## Problem and fix

#4090 accelerated `CreateNetsFromProps`, but its separate existence index did not help later `selectOne("net.NAME", { type: "net" })` calls in vias and traces. The complete render still performed the expensive tree scans. My earlier lookup-only benchmark missed this shift.

Restore `createNetsFromProps` to its original `selectOne` call and move the optimization into shared literal-net resolution. Creation, source traces, vias and pours now resolve through the same scoped index. The index keys off the cached `selectAll("net")` array, so existing ancestor add/remove invalidation rebuilds it. It preserves the first matching net/alias, subcircuit boundaries and misses, respects type constraints before consulting an untyped result cache, and leaves complex/invalid selectors on the existing validation/CSS path.

## Representative benchmark

Replace the lookup-only script with a full `renderUntilSettled()` fixture, also registered in the browser benchmark suite: 1,500 placed parts, 3,000 source traces, 1,500 connected vias, 1,500 pre-routed PCB traces and 1,054 nets. No autorouting or pours. Includes declared and implicitly-created net variants, board-level phase timing, inventories, error detection and full-output SHA-256.

Three fresh sequential processes per declared variant, same dependencies; median local timings:

| Variant | Entire core benchmark | Net creation phase | Source trace phase |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original lookup behavior | 16.13 s | 8.81 s | 0.10 s |
| Released #4090 | 13.96 s | 0.06 s | 7.59 s |
| This replacement | **6.92 s** | 0.07 s | **0.18 s** |

The original-lookup control restores the pre-#4090 call in the otherwise identical release bundle. All nine runs produce **identical hashes and 32,558 records**. The implicit-net sanity comparison also preserves identical output (14.89 s → 12.10 s, one run each).

**Actual AM62A import through eval, pours off:** median local Node evaluation **28.38 s → 12.02 s**, core rendering **25.77 s → 9.97 s**, three fresh processes each. All six outputs preserve the same 66,347 records and hash after excluding only version metadata, with zero pours/errors. Both bundles receive the same existing app compatibility patches; no synthetic cache warming or per-component diagnostic listeners are enabled. These are local measurements, not a production-deployment claim.

Commands, methodology, samples and hashes are committed under `benchmarking/scripts/net-resolution-*`.

## Validation

- `bun run build` and `bunx tsc --noEmit`.
- Relevant selector, base-component, net-name, via, trace-connectivity, shared/exposed-net, copper-pour and group-port tests: **112 passed, 2 existing skips; 5 snapshots unchanged**.
- New cross-phase test fails against released behavior (101 alias scans instead of one), passes with this fix.
- Regression coverage includes typed/untyped reuse, wrong-type requests, duplicate/whitespace aliases, cached misses, ordinary-group ancestor invalidation, nested subcircuit isolation and complex selectors.

title: Avoid repeated CSS tree searches when creating declared nets
description: Reduces the time spent in createNetsFromProps by indexing literal net selectors, significantly improving performance for large imported boards.
body:
Large imported boards spend substantial time in `createNetsFromProps`: each previously unseen `net.NAME` selector walks the component tree through `css-select`, even when all nets are explicitly declared. Profiling the AM62A reference board with pours disabled attributed about 9.2 seconds (41% of sampled CPU time) to this path.

Index literal net selectors from the existing subcircuit-scoped `selectAll("net")` result. A WeakMap keys the index by that cached result array, so the existing ancestor cache invalidation rebuilds it after add/remove operations. Non-literal selectors retain the CSS lookup, and validation and class-alias matching remain intact. No application-specific flags or lifecycle listeners are required.

### Validation

- `bun run build`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- Relevant base-component, selector, net-name, shared/exposed-net, and group-port tests: **95 passed, 2 existing skips**, including 3 new regression tests.
- `bun benchmarking/scripts/benchmark-net-creation.ts`: **2,524 ms → 11.3 ms** for the cold net-creation lookup step on a tree with 1,500 chips, 15,000 ports, and 1,000 declared nets. Each strategy starts with a fresh tree and verifies that the original net instances are preserved. This is a targeted microbenchmark, not a whole-render speedup.

The regression tests exercise cache reuse, ordinary-group ancestor invalidation, automatic net creation, subcircuit isolation, duplicate names, whitespace class aliases, complex selector fallback, and invalid net names. They assert selector/tree behavior directly because these cache semantics are not visible in a PCB snapshot; existing rendering snapshots remain unchanged.

title: Preserve regional proposals when clearance projection violates the via guard
description: Preserves negotiated routes during regional rerouting when clearance projection would invalidate them due to via guard violations.
body:
Regional rerouting can change a route's point indices while retaining an existing physical via. Clearance projection validates against that intermediate route, so it can move an existing via-to-pad contact and accept the projection. The outer repair guard compares against the pre-reroute geometry, cannot establish the same via correspondence, and rejects the entire regional proposal—including the useful negotiated route.

Pass the pre-reroute routes into clearance projection and use them as its via-guard reference. Both guards now assess the same transition. If projection would invalidate the proposal, its existing rejection path preserves the negotiated routes for outer validation. Whole-board trace and via movement remains available. The outer physical guards, full reference DRC, and incomplete-repair publication policy remain enforced.

- All 15 local tests pass (214 assertions), including the new physical-geometry regression and full-board SRJ18 samples 2, 4, and 13. The new test fails against main.

The candidate shares an eight-rerip budget with the parent search. This lets sample 6 finish its graph while skipping repeated search on boards such as sample 14 that have already spent that budget. Existing greedy orders and budgets remain unchanged. No DRC tolerances, benchmark settings, or timeouts change.

This PR changes only the dependency pin. Implementation and regression test: https://github.com/tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph/pull/211 (stacked on #207, which the autorouter already pins).

title: fix: precheck reachability before selective blocker search
description: Adds a reachability check to prevent unnecessary rerouting attempts in the solver when a route is blocked by another route, specifically addressing issues in the routing process for board107-1726.
body:
For board107-1726—the input currently in the PR—the disconnection is created by a rerouting decision:
1. Route 669 occupies a narrow area that route 670 also needs.
2. The solver tries moving 669 to make room for 670.
3. The routes repeatedly interfere with each other, creating a rerouting cycle.
4. To try a different solution, the solver asks: “Can I route 670 without moving 669?”
5. Keeping 669 fixed blocks all seven modeled exits around cmn_1134, isolating the target at cmn_2785.
The original graph has those connections. But the graph of moves allowed for that particular attempt is disconnected. Removing any number of other traces cannot help because 669 blocks the necessary access.
That is why the check belongs in tiny-hypergraph: it tests whether its own proposed constraint—“don’t move 669”—makes the search impossible.
The underlying conflict happens because routing is incremental. A route chosen earlier can occupy access needed by a later route. The solver must then reconsider those choices. The reachability check rejects an impossible alternative; it doesn’t solve the ordering or shared-corridor problem by itself.

**So, for the current board107-1726 test, the main explanation is an impossible constrained rerouting attempt, rather than an incorrectly constructed initial graph. A deeper routing improvement would reconsider the two conflicting routes together or their routing order; the current tiny-hypergraph fix prevents wasting minutes on an alternative that cannot work.**


This PR now targets main directly and excludes #207. It includes the regression test from #210 with the fixed snapshot so the fix is independently mergeable. Validation without #207: all 8 focused blocker-search and reachability tests pass (41 assertions). Full board107 routing has not been rerun on this revised commit.

title: Replace smoothstep with quadratic teardrop interpolation
description: Replaces smoothstep with quadratic interpolation for teardrop width transitions, updating schema and validation tests accordingly.
body:
Replace `smoothstep` with `quadratic` for concave teardrops that flatten into the narrow trace. The supported modes are now `linear` and `quadratic`; existing `smoothstep` inputs fail schema validation.

Measure u from the wide end toward the narrow end:

`w(u) = narrow_width + (wide_width - narrow_width) * (1-u)^2`

In route order, the interpolation fraction is `t²` when widening and `2t-t²` when narrowing. This keeps the narrow-end tangent flat and preserves the copper geometry when endpoints and widths are reversed. Equal widths remain a constant-width segment. The profile does not imply tangency to a pad at its wide end.

Updates the schema, TypeScript interface, README, geometry contract, and parsing/round-trip tests for both supported profiles, including explicit rejection of the removed mode. Renderer follow-ups: tscircuit/circuit-to-svg#783, tscircuit/circuit-to-canvas#295, tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu#6.

title: Add teardrop route segments with endpoint widths and interpolation
description: Add a new route type teardrop to represent tapered wire segments with varying widths in PCB traces, enhancing the geometry representation without requiring separate copper pours.
body:
Represent teardrops directly in `pcb_trace.route` as straight wire segments with a varying full copper width. This makes the geometry explicit without representing each taper as an independently solved copper pour.

```json
{
  "route_type": "teardrop",
  "start": { "x": 0, "y": 0 },
  "end": { "x": 0.8, "y": 0 },
  "start_width": 0.6,
  "end_width": 0.2,
  "width_interpolation_mode": "smoothstep",
  "layer": "top"
}
```

`start_width` / `end_width` follow existing wire `width` naming; explicit `start` / `end` follow the `through_pad` segment convention. Coordinates and full widths use millimeters, with unit strings accepted as schema inputs.

Two profiles are defined precisely: `linear` uses f(t)=t, while `smoothstep` uses f(t)=3t²−2t³ for zero width derivative at both ends. The local profile is independent of trace-level `route_thickness_mode`. Both widening and narrowing segments are supported. Widths must be positive and finite, and endpoints must define a finite, nonzero length.

The [geometry and traversal specification](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/blob/feat/pcb-trace-teardrops/docs/pcb-trace-teardrops.md) defines boundaries, caps, route adjacency, layer changes, length, and optional port/pour annotations. There is no polygon variant or trace-level teardrop array.

This draft adds the schema, exported TypeScript interface, documentation, and tests. Existing documents remain valid, but consumers need explicit handling for the new route type. Core/router generation, rendering, DRC, solver obstacle conversion, and fabrication export are follow-up work; this schema alone does not improve pour performance.

title: Avoid self-short false positives at short routed bends
description: Fixes false positive self-short reports for valid AM62L DQ0 fanout bends due to floating-point roundoff and local copper overlap.
body:
The self-short check reports valid AM62L DQ0 fanout bends as shorts, causing tscircuit/core#4108 to fail. At one tiny chamfer, floating-point roundoff makes perpendicular directions have a slightly negative dot product. At another short stepped bend, the connecting path is slightly longer than the copper width even though the overlap is local to the bend.

Scale the directional tolerance by the segment lengths and allow a right-angle connector's sqrt(2) path-length factor for local forward-facing overlap. Reversing legs remain checked, preserving narrow hairpin detection. Add regressions using the actual failing coordinates.

Validation: all 20 focused self-short tests pass, including crossing, hairpin, retracing, and via-contact regressions. The exported AM62L circuit no longer reports a self-short. All 439 tests, type check, and package build pass.

The previously failing core AM62L regression also passes against this fix (12,981 assertions), with its existing visual snapshot unchanged. All five upstream PR CI checks pass.

title: Detect self-shorts in length-matched PCB traces
description: Adds a check for self-shorts in length-matched PCB traces, enhancing routing checks to prevent shorts across their own routes.
body:
The trace overlap check skips electrically connected segments, allowing a length-matched PCB trace to short across its own route without reporting an error. Add `checkPcbTraceSelfShorts` and include it in the existing overlap check, which also makes it part of routing checks.

Detect same-layer wire crossings, copper-width contact, immediately retraced segments, and route vias whose copper contacts a distant section of their own trace. Via checks use the materialized via geometry when available, or the route via diameter and board layer span. Preserve normal corners, short subdivisions, via entry/exit connections, and crossings on different layers. Emit one error per affected PCB trace with a contact location and readable trace or endpoint names, never raw IDs in the diagnostic message.

The visual regression shows a 0.7 mm via land touching a nearby 0.25 mm trace without any centerline crossing. Shrinking only the via copper clears the error. The SVG keeps the contact visible and displays the readable diagnostic below the route.

Scope is traces belonging to a `source_bus` with `max_length_skew`: the current Circuit JSON schema has no impedance constraint field. Checks operate within each PCB trace and its route vias; pad-mediated shorts and contact across separate PCB trace fragments remain outside this change.

- TypeScript check, formatting, and package build passed.
- Rendered and visually inspected the updated SVG snapshot.

title: Retain safe nudges from existing Pipeline9 clearance projection
description: Retains safe wire nudges during autorouting while preventing unrelated trace errors from blocking repairs, improving overall error counts in the routing process.
body:
Pipeline9 already generates useful trace nudges, but its bounded repair phase discards partial progress while unrelated trace/via errors remain. A lower total error count alone is also insufficient: the whole-board projection can worsen other gaps.

Use the existing `applyPipeline9ClearanceProjection` / repair04 `relaxTraceClearance` in a guarded partial-repair mode. It keeps drill sites fixed and uses the existing clearance margin. Select only route proposals whose changed segments are clear of all foreign copper and the board bounds, including previously accepted proposals. Preserve repair04's terminal/junction locks, point widths, and the original explicit via metadata. The full reference checker must then confirm fewer errors with no new or worsened remaining error identities; unknown/continuity errors still prevent partial publication.

`applyPipeline9BoundedRegionalRepairs` first runs its existing coupled projection and regional search, including via movement, with unchanged acceptance rules and work budgets. If that search cannot publish a result, it selects independently safe wire nudges from the original input. This keeps the partial-repair constraints from blocking complete coupled repairs, and prevents private regional proposals from leaking into the published partial result. Matched nets remain protected, and unsupported copper is excluded from partial projection.

All movement comes from the existing projection. The separate `LocalDrcRepairSolver`, its bespoke nudge and via-merge algorithms, and its HD coordinate-transfer adapter are removed. The existing same-net via merger and regional reroute guards remain unchanged. No pipeline stage, dependency, clearance rule, or CI workflow is changed; there are no board-specific cases or WeakMaps.

### Bugreport107

Complete local routing run on macOS arm64 / Bun 1.3.14:

| Output | Benchmark DRC errors |
| --- | ---: |
| Before the projection fix | 141 |
| Joint DRC output | 107 |
| Final output after power expansion | **104** |

The existing repair path removes 20 pad–trace clearance errors, 9 via–trace clearance errors, and 5 overlap errors. Power expansion removes another 3 via–trace errors. Final output improves from the previously measured unmodified baseline of 138 errors to 104. The remaining 104 errors include 9 via-spacing errors; this change does not claim to clear the board.

With the board's declared clearances, counts are 178 → 144 → 139. Independent geometry audits found no new/worsened pairwise violations across either the repair or subsequent power expansion. Physical-connectivity audits passed for both outputs, covering 1,916 endpoint instances.

### Validation

- Full bugreport107 routing test passed; updated board snapshot was visually inspected and verified again from the saved production output without snapshot updates.
- 31 focused tests passed: mixed pad/via errors, retained partial progress, neighboring conflicts, branch contacts, matched nets, reference rejection, existing repair behavior, preloads, and downstream length matching/power expansion.
- TypeScript checking and production build passed.
- SRJ18 repair close-ups match the original main-branch snapshots again; their remaining input overlap is still reported.
- `bun-test.yml` is unchanged, and bugreport107 retains its original test timeout.

The measured routing run took 404 seconds, including 47 seconds in joint DRC and 110 seconds in power expansion, with other validation work running concurrently. This is not a speed claim. The formatting-only follow-up passes the repository formatting check across all 1,594 files in a clean checkout.


### CI regression fixes

Keep the original coupled projection (including via movement) and regional search ahead of independent wire-only repair. The wire-only mode had prevented repairs that required moving a via and changed the regional search input. Both full SRJ18 sample-2 tests now pass locally with zero DRC errors; their original search-budget assertions remain unchanged. The full bugreport107 rerun also passes: both its pre-power copper and final output are identical to the previously audited result. A focused regression fails on the previous implementation and passes on this revision.

Bugreport107's Linux run passed its DRC assertions but produced a different native route variant (103 final errors versus 104 on macOS). Follow the repository's existing platform-specific snapshot convention using the inspected Linux CI artifact, with the original snapshot tolerance and identical DRC assertions on both platforms. Original SRJ18 close-up snapshots are restored. No workflow or timeout changes.

title: Simplify label detours and attach rail labels to clear corners
description: Simplifies the Allwinner T113 upper LDOA1V8 supply trace by reducing bends from 24 to 2 and directly attaching the power label to its clear upper corner, enhancing trace efficiency and label placement.
body:
The Allwinner T113 upper LDOA1V8 supply trace takes separate detours around successive labels, leaving 24 bends where a continuous outer rail needs only two. Its power label also remains on a generated connector at the lower end after the outer rail becomes clear. This change simplifies the rail to two bends and places the label directly on its clear upper corner.

Late trace cleanup accepts shorter interior shortcuts and revisits a trace until no further simplification is valid. The early equivalent-length pass retains its existing contract because turn minimization and label placement follow it. Candidates preserve terminal directions, label anchors, and same-net junctions, and use the existing component, label, other-net overlap, and crossing checks.

The existing rail corner-placement solver now considers newly exposed corners for labels attached through generated connectors. It uses the connector registry and the label's trace associations to find the host rail. A connector can be removed only if every shared junction, physical pin, and other label attachment remains on that rail. Corner selection reuses the existing ordering and collision checks without rerouting the rail for this placement. There are no board-specific conditions or new point-count heuristics.

The captured Core-input Allwinner repro is already on main and its JSON is unchanged. Added assertions check two bends, preserved pin connections, direct attachment at the upper corner, and removal of the redundant connector. The bend assertion fails on main; the label assertion fails on the previous PR revision. The robot-controller repro checks electrical connectivity for both direct and connector-backed label attachments.

Validation: **469 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed in CI**; typecheck, repository formatting, and package build passed. Both gamepad snapshots and the smart-lock snapshots remain unchanged. All eight changed snapshots were reviewed. Comparing output-label collisions before and after the connector-placement change found no new collisions in its four affected fixtures.

Earlier simplification leaves one cycle for the repeated-junction cleanup instead of two; both junctions still align, and its expected stage count is updated accordingly.

title: Use pver for automatic TI npm releases
description: Switches the TI npm release process to use pver for automatic versioning and publishing on main branch pushes or manual dispatch, improving the release workflow.
body:
## Summary

TI currently publishes only when an `npm-v*` tag is pushed. Switch to the pver release process used by `tscircuit` / `@tscircuit/cli`: release on `main` pushes or manual dispatch, push a version tag, publish to npm, then create a version-bump PR and enable squash auto-merge.

TI has two package identities, so use `pver release --git --package-json --no-push-main` to version/tag the root without publishing it, then explicitly publish the tested `dist/npm` distribution as `@tscircuit/ti`. The build now copies the root version into the npm manifest; the template no longer maintains a second version. Package tests verify the packed and globally installed versions against the root manifest.

Serialize releases, fetch full Git history, skip version-bump merge commits, and skip publication when pver detects no new version. Add the previously missing publishing guide, including first publication, OIDC configuration, bot access, and retry behavior.

## Validation

- `bun install --no-save` succeeded (an initial transient npm tarball 404 cleared on retry).
- `bun run test:cli`: 9 Node tests and the imported-component schematic snapshot passed.
- `bun run build:npm` and `bun run test:npm` passed, including clean local/global installs, CLI search/import, ESM/CJS, declaration checks, and `tsci build`.
- `bun run format:check`, actionlint 1.7.12, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Exercised published pver 0.0.43 against a temporary local bare Git remote with npm invocation blocked: version bump/tag succeeded, remote main remained unchanged, no-change rerun skipped, and retry skipped an existing tag.

## Release setup

Before automatic publication, provide `TSCIRCUIT_BOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, enable repository auto-merge, bootstrap `@tscircuit/ti` if it has not been published, and configure npm trusted publishing for `tscircuit/ti` with workflow filename `npm-publish.yml`. These external setup steps are documented in `docs/npm-publishing.md`; this PR does not publish a package.

## Summary

Implement the Canvas 2D subset needed to render Circuit JSON directly to RGBA/PNG through `circuit-to-canvas`, without SVG rasterization, native runtime dependencies, or WASM.

The rasterizer supports polygon fills, even-odd holes, arcs/ellipses/arcTo, transformed strokes with caps/joins/dashes, nested clipping, alpha compositing, and non-repeating canvas patterns for offscreen soldermask layers. `createCanvas({ width, height })` provides image data, PNG bytes, and PNG data URLs. Unsupported features such as system-font text, gradients, and image decoding are explicitly outside this subset; PCB lettering uses glyph paths.

This follows the existing series-inductor exception: the solver avoids imposing one orientation when the component continues a power path rather than forming a rail branch. ## Ref This schematic shows that a diode connecting two power nets can be placed vertically. It also contains horizontally placed power-path diodes, showing that one fixed orientation is not correct for every series power diode. title: Render linear and quadratic teardrops on wire segments
description: Render linear and quadratic teardrops using optional taper fields on ordinary pcb_trace.route wire points, preserving neighboring segments and avoiding duplicate strokes.
body:
Render linear and quadratic teardrops using optional taper fields on ordinary `pcb_trace.route` wire points. A taper belongs to the outgoing segment from that point to the next wire, via, or through-pad, with no separate route type or duplicate anchors.

```json
[
  { "route_type": "wire", "x": 0, "y": 0, "layer": "top", "width": 0.6,
    "start_width": 0.6, "end_width": 0.2, "width_interpolation_mode": "quadratic" },
  { "route_type": "wire", "x": 0.8, "y": 0, "layer": "top", "width": 0.2 }
]
```

Preserves neighboring ordinary segments and avoids a duplicate stroke over the taper. Quadratic is concave with a flat tangent at the narrow end; reversing endpoints and widths preserves its shape. Smoothstep is unsupported. Tessellation has a bounded error and bounded vertex count. Invalid tapers produce no geometry.

Schema: https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/830. A local wire extension type supports the pending fields without depending on an unpublished package.

The demo covers linear and quadratic profiles, pad/wire/via joins, rotation, and multiple layers. No copper pours are needed.

![Wire taper demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/feat/teardrop-routes/tests/pcb/__snapshots__/teardrop-trace.snap.svg)

body:
Closely spaced merges start release jobs from the same package version. After one job pushes its version bump, the other can fail when pver rebases its own version change onto main.

Add a shared concurrency group with `cancel-in-progress: false` so release jobs run one at a time. Check out current `main` when a queued job starts so it includes the preceding release's version bump.

Only `.github/workflows/pver-release.yml` changes. The existing build and publish steps are preserved; `package.json` has no changes.

title: Fix connectivity crash near rounded trace ends
description: Fixes a crash in connectivity checking when a via is near the rounded end of a trace with separated copper.
body:
Connectivity checking can crash when a via is near the rounded end of a trace but their copper is separated. `getViaPolygon(..., 0)` creates a zero-radius inner arc, and Flatten's arc-distance calculation dereferences a missing intersection point.

Construct the existing solid barrel contact envelope directly with `circlePolygon`. This preserves the intended outer-copper geometry and layer-span handling without creating a degenerate hole. A regression covers separated and touching copper for both explicit vias and vias embedded in trace routes.

Validation: 512 tests pass, TypeScript passes, and the package builds. Reproduced while validating tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#2735 on the RP2040 motor-controller regression. Kept separate from the hole-clearance feature.

title: Keep hole geometry independent of the electrical layer stack
description: Fixes hole clearance checks by ensuring NPTH geometry is validated independently of the electrical layer stack, preventing false failures in multi-layer boards.
body:
The hole overlap/clearance checks currently pass the entire circuit to the Flatten converter. Its electrical layer-stack validation runs before the element-type filter, so a board with more than ten layers throws even when it has no non-plated holes. This breaks existing SRJ29 autorouter regressions after upgrading checks.

Convert only `pcb_hole` elements when extracting physical hole boundaries. NPTH geometry is independent of the board's electrical layer stack; strict hole-geometry validation and the clearance calculation are unchanged. Extend the existing hole-clearance test with a 12-layer board, both without holes and with a violating hole/trace pair.

Validation: the new case fails before the fix; all 511 tests, TypeScript, and the package build pass after it. Follow-up to #340, found while validating tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#2735.

title: Check trace-to-hole edge clearance using board and manufacturing rules
description: Adds checkHoleTraceClearance in check-hole-trace-clearance.ts to measure copper-edge distance to physical non-plated holes, integrating with existing routing checks and ensuring compliance with defined clearance rules.
body:
Adds `checkHoleTraceClearance` in `check-hole-trace-clearance.ts`, following the existing `checkPadTraceClearance` naming and integration pattern. The rule measures copper-edge distance to physical non-plated holes, using an explicit override, then `pcb_board.min_trace_to_hole_edge_clearance`, then the JLCPCB 0.2 mm minimum.

`runAllRoutingChecks` calls hole clearance alongside pad and via clearance. `checkEachPcbTraceNonOverlapping` retains physical hole-overlap detection and returns only its own errors; it does not invoke the clearance check or accept a separate hole-clearance option. Shared hole geometry keeps circle, square, rectangle, oval, pill and rotated-pill classification consistent. As with pad/via checks, an overlapping trace/hole pair is excluded from clearance results so it is reported only once.

The overlap check includes wire-to-via segments so moving physical overlap detection there preserves coverage at trace endpoints. Existing keyboard expectations distinguish overlap and clearance results; two previously omitted wire-to-via contacts are now detected in keyboard1.

The existing hole regression covers copper width, layers, shape geometry, board/explicit overrides and overlap-versus-clearance deduplication. Its PCB SVG snapshot shows a 0.15 mm gap failing and a 0.20 mm gap passing. The snapshot also verifies integration through `runAllRoutingChecks`.

Validation: all 510 tests pass (5,736 assertions), TypeScript checking and build pass. Supports tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#2735. The independent endpoint port-inference fix is in #341.

title: Respect copper layers when inferring trace endpoint ports
description: Fixes false missing-via errors by requiring trace endpoint ports to match the copper layer of the associated pads before inferring their IDs.
body:
A trace endpoint without a port ID can overlap a pad on the opposite copper layer. Endpoint inference currently uses only XY position, so a top-layer waypoint above a bottom-only pad acquires that pad's port ID and produces a false missing-via error.

Require the wire's layer to match the port's layers or the SMD pad's layer before inferring its ID. Explicit endpoint IDs remain unchanged, and multilayer ports still connect on their supported layers. The regression covers direct port matches, off-center pad matches, multilayer ports, and explicit IDs.

Validation: all 510 tests pass (5,583 assertions), TypeScript checking and build pass.

Discovered while validating the Corne left half for tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#2735. This fix is independent of the hole-clearance check in #340.

title: Render linear and quadratic teardrops on wire segments
description: Render linear and quadratic teardrops using optional taper fields on ordinary pcb_trace.route wire points, preserving neighboring segments and avoiding duplicate strokes.
body:
Render linear and quadratic teardrops using optional taper fields on ordinary `pcb_trace.route` wire points. A taper belongs to the outgoing segment from that point to the next wire, via, or through-pad, with no separate route type or duplicate anchors.

```json
[
  { "route_type": "wire", "x": 0, "y": 0, "layer": "top", "width": 0.6,
    "start_width": 0.6, "end_width": 0.2, "width_interpolation_mode": "quadratic" },
  { "route_type": "wire", "x": 0.8, "y": 0, "layer": "top", "width": 0.2 }
]
```

Preserves neighboring ordinary segments and avoids a duplicate stroke over the taper. Quadratic is concave with a flat tangent at the narrow end; reversing endpoints and widths preserves its shape. Smoothstep is unsupported. Tessellation has a bounded error and bounded vertex count. Invalid tapers produce no geometry.

Schema: https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/830. A local wire extension type supports the pending fields without depending on an unpublished package.

The demo covers linear and quadratic profiles, pad/wire/via joins, rotation, and multiple layers. No copper pours are needed.

![Wire taper demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-canvas/feat/teardrop-routes/tests/elements/__snapshots__/teardrop-trace.snap.png)

Validation: 179 tests passed, plus the added incoming/outgoing neighbor regression; TypeScript and build passed. PNG snapshot remains unchanged.

title: Add 0.2 mm NPTH-to-trace clearance to JLCPCB tolerances
description: Add min_trace_to_hole_edge_clearance: 0.2 mm to jlcMinTolerances and jlcPreferredTolerances for JLCPCB specifications.
body:
Add `min_trace_to_hole_edge_clearance: 0.2` mm to `jlcMinTolerances` and `jlcPreferredTolerances`. JLCPCB's [PCB capabilities](https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities) lists **NPTH to Track: 0.2 mm** under Traces. The preferred map uses the same documented minimum for this rule.

Update the Circuit JSON development dependency to 0.0.506, which defines this `PcbBoard` field, and document the trace-copper-edge to non-plated-hole-edge measurement.

Validation: typecheck, formatting/lint check, and a runtime check of both exported maps pass. Biome emits existing configuration-version/deprecation informational messages.

Follow-up: core can consume this value as its manufacturer default using the same nullish fallback as other clearances in https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4153. This PR supplies the specification; it does not change core's dependency or default yet.

title: Reproduce missing copper polygon cutouts
description: Reproduces the issue where linked polygon cutouts on a polygon without a poured copper region suppress the polygon entirely, leading to missing copper geometry in the conversion process.
body: ## Motivation Two Altium polygon-cutout cases currently lose copper geometry: - A linked `POLYGON_CUTOUT` on a polygon without a poured `COPPER` region suppresses the polygon entirely. The small fixture records this as zero `pcb_copper_pour` elements. - The [MIT-licensed CH582 board](https://github.com/iot-lorawan/CH582_PCB_SCH/blob/b65bce802295c6c40413c5bc3ea54682820619c1/PCB_ch582_2022-06-16.pcbdoc) has two polygon pours and four unlinked cutouts (two on each copper layer). The converter retains the pours but omits their holes. ## Reference : ## Reproduction Pin the CH582 source by commit and SHA-256 in the reference manifest, then add a full-board side-by-side bottom-copper snapshot. The `altiumts` source rendering shows the openings; the Circuit JSON rendering fills them with copper. The test asserts that the current bottom pour is a plain polygon. [View the CH582 before snapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KrishnaX12/altium-to-circuit-json/5c5957e/tests/svg/__snapshots__/ch582-polygon-cutouts.snap.svg). The minimal linked-cutout fixture separately snapshots the polygon disappearing. [View that before snapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KrishnaX12/altium-to-circuit-json/5c5957e/tests/conversion/__snapshots__/pcb-polygon-cutout.snap.svg). This Draft PR contains only reproductions; the converter fix and after snapshot are in #68.
